# A process has a rank and a lifetime

[Start MPI once, query its communicator and turn rank-local values into a global answer.]{.lesson-deck}
:::

Parallel C++ begins with a small lifetime question: who starts MPI, and who
finishes it? OpenPFC's environment wrapper owns those calls for a standalone
program. A communicator then supplies the rank and group size.

```{.cpp include="model.cpp" snippet="ownership" dedent=2}
```

The local value is the rank $r$. The collective sums all ranks, so the
independent answer is

$$\sum_{r=0}^{P-1}r=P(P-1)/2.$$

Every rank participates in the collective; only rank zero prints the result.
Root-only output does not make the collective a root-only operation.

## Run the same program with a different process count

```sh
openpfc run model.cpp input.json --launcher=none
openpfc run model.cpp input.json --ranks=2 --launcher=mpirun
```

The empty input is unused. The printed CSV reports `ranks` and `rank_sum`.
The tests check $P=1$ and $P=2$. Changing the rank count changes the sum,
not the source code or an assumed constant inside it.

The environment must be constructed before communicator operations and
outlive them. Its constructor calls `MPI_Init` and its destructor calls
`MPI_Finalize`; do not add a second owner in a host application that already
initialised MPI. Use the host's lifetime and pass its communicator in that
case. A duplicated communicator manages a communication context, not a
second MPI runtime. Continue with a
[class-owned session](../session/index.qmd), or inspect the public
[environment wrapper](https://github.com/VTT-ProperTune/OpenPFC/blob/master/include/openpfc/kernel/mpi/environment.hpp).

The complete [C++ model](model.cpp) and [starting input](input.json)
are available with this lesson.
